description: The app from inside: requests, routes, database queries, cache, and the Node.js process.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: Requests the API answered per second, all routes. The metrics endpoint itself is not counted.

panels.title: Server errors (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests that ended in a 5xx: a fault on the server side. Above 5%, with at least 5 errors in 5 minutes, fires AppHighErrorRate.

panels.title: Client errors (4xx)
panels.description: Share of requests refused as the client's mistake: missing or expired token (401), validation (422), not found (404), rate limited (429). Some are normal; a sudden rise often means a frontend or client bug.

panels.title: Latency p95
panels.description: 95% of requests finished faster than this. Above 1s for 10 minutes, with real traffic, fires AppHighLatency.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Requests being handled right now. Climbing and not coming down means requests are stuck waiting (on the database or Redis).

panels.title: App
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape the app. DOWN for 2 minutes fires AppDown.

panels.title: Requests by status
panels.description: Per second, by status class. 4xx is normal in small amounts; 5xx should be flat at 0.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: p50: a typical request. p95 and p99: the slow ones, which users notice. A p99 far above p95 usually points at one slow route (see below).

panels.title: Endpoints
panels.description: Per route over the selected time range. Paths are route patterns (/users/:id), so ids don't multiply the rows; "unmatched" is requests to routes that don't exist.

targets.expr: sum by (method, path) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum{job="nestjs-app"}[$__range])) / sum by (method, path) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="nestjs-app"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Busiest routes
panels.description: Top 10 routes by requests per second.

panels.title: Slowest routes (p95)
panels.description: Top 10 routes by p95 latency. A route that only gets a few requests can look slow from a single one.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, path) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="nestjs-app"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0)

panels.title: Sign-ins
panels.description: Successful sign-ins in the selected range, with a password or with Google.

panels.title: Failed sign-ins
panels.description: Wrong passwords and unknown addresses in the selected range (alert: AuthFailedLoginSpike at 50 in 10 minutes).

panels.title: Refused by the limits
panels.description: Sign-ins refused because an address or network tried too often (docs/auth/rate-limits.md).

panels.title: Refresh token reuse
panels.description: Sessions ended because a refresh token came back after it was replaced: usually a copied cookie (alert: AuthRefreshTokenReuse).

panels.title: Sign-in attempts
panels.description: Every sign-in outcome per minute.

panels.title: Account changes
panels.description: Registrations, password resets and deletions per minute.

panels.title: Queries / s
panels.description: Prisma queries per second, from the app. Postgres' own view is the Postgres dashboard.

panels.title: Query p95
panels.description: 95% of Prisma queries took less than this, including the wait for a free pool connection.

panels.title: Cache hit rate
panels.description: Share of reads served from the cache, per cache. auth_session: the session checked on every signed-in request; auth_user: the signed-in user read with it. Misses read the database. Only signed-in requests use them.

panels.title: Cache reads / s
panels.description: Cache lookups per second, hits and misses together.

panels.title: Queries by operation
panels.description: Prisma operations per second (findUnique, update, ...).

panels.title: Query p95 by operation
panels.description: Slow operations stand out here; the Postgres dashboard shows whether the database or the pool is the cause.

panels.title: Cache hits and misses
panels.description: Per cache, per second.

panels.title: Event loop lag (p99)
panels.description: How late timers and I/O callbacks run. Every request waits this long on top of its own work; above 0.5s for 5 minutes fires AppEventLoopLag.

panels.title: Memory (RSS)
panels.description: Memory the process holds. The production container is limited to 512 MB: past it the kernel kills the app (alert: HostOutOfMemoryKill).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of one core the process uses. Node.js runs JavaScript on one thread: near 100% means it is saturated, whatever the number of cores.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Process starts in the selected range: deploys, crashes, or kills for memory (alert: AppRestarting at 3 in 30 minutes).

panels.title: Event loop lag
panels.description: Median and p99. Spikes line up with CPU-heavy synchronous work (image processing, big JSON).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: rss: all memory the process holds. heap used: JavaScript objects; if it only grows across hours, something leaks. external: buffers outside the heap (uploads, image processing).

title: NestJS API Metrics
